title: bls12-381-g1-ecdlp-plain: parallel Pollard rho on order-6 classes with a sigma walk, all arithmetic in instructions

claims.statement: For uniform x in [0,r) and input T=[x]P0 in BLS12-381 G1 the parallel distinguished-point Pollard rho algorithm in proof.md recovers x with probability at least 0.39. It walks on the order-6 classes {±1, ±λ, ±λ²} of G1, using 2^30 walks and 2^16 adders, with batched affine additions. Walks run in trails from fresh coins: each trail ends at its first distinguished point, which it records once, including a distinguished point first reached during a look-ahead, and the first key match is resolved by replaying both trails, so a degenerate match has probability exactly 1/r (Lemmas R and D). Fruitless cycles are escaped only after exact checks, and the distinguished-point test comes first on every point produced. A fruitless cycle is escaped to twice the canonical point of its least-key member, a doubling with no table. The formal structure (D1, D2) gives that an escape point is not formally equal to any earlier point of its trail, under the check ord_r(2) > 3*TRAIL_MAX, which holds for this r: ord_r(2) = (r-1)/16, about 2^250.86 (proof.md section 2.3). Within-trail coincidences, degenerate or not, have probability at most DELTA_LOOP = 1.56e-16 (section 2.4), and a trail is abandoned with probability at most 1.82e-28 (Lemma T', section 2.6), which gives DELTA_ABANDON = 2.83e-17. Total computation is at most 2^126.390705 target-group-operation equivalents, including preprocessing, distinguished-point storage and lookup, all failures and restarts, collision replay, verification and output. Each walk step pays its common-path count, 2263 instructions, and a Markov reserve of 53.91 for rare work. The expected rare work is E_RARE = 0.842324 per step: the 2-cycle and anchor checks, the exact-k fallback at 2^-55 per canon call with worst case 682 instructions, and the within-trail coincidence row. That is 2316.91 instructions per walk step at C=2000. Rare work is charged at forced-path maxima, measured with a bounding build of each unbatched operation, and the meter aborts when the metered rare work exceeds 64 times its expectation, with probability at most 1/64 (counted in delta). Peak memory is at most 2^75.178504 bytes. Preprocessing is at most 2^46.934918 units and is included in total work. Nonuniform advice is 0 bytes. This is a classical cold attack on one target with no uncharged advice or quantum steps. The success bound of 0.395898 is the model bound 0.411524 less 1/64 for the meter, 2^-20 for the H1 terms and the degenerate match, DELTA_ABANDON and DELTA_LOOP. It relies on the disclosed premises in proof.md: H1 (the standard random-mapping model for r-adding class walks, used for collision statistics only); M1 (class data, including the canonical coordinate fractions, are independent and uniform per class, independent of x; this gives the closure rates, Lemma G, Lemma T', Lemma M' and the fallback rate); and M2 (the table is fixed by the seed random.Random(1) of the specification with the stream position of proof.md section 2.2, and behaves as uniform values independent of x; probabilities are over the uniform target x; a second premise). H3 is the representativeness of the measured instruction counts of the common path, with rare work charged at forced-path maxima. These are supported by toy-curve runs of the identical procedure and by production-curve measurements, not proved. The argument is not established at production size. This is a carefully accounted generic attack, not a claim of a practical break.

experiments.purpose: Run the complete procedure of proof.md section 1.3 on toy curves y^2=x^3+4 in prime-order subgroups (b=4, the BLS12-381 G1 shape) or prime-order y^2=x^3+7 (b=7), at budget tau = tau_e4/10^4: each slot runs trails from fresh coins without tracking coefficients, with the same class key, canonical rule, adder images and index, both cycle rules and escapes; a trail ends at its first distinguished point, recorded once with its coins, or is abandoned at the cap; each slot takes L steps and finishes its trail. The first key match is resolved by replaying both trails from their coins (with a different anchor schedule, checking Lemma R); a degenerate match fails. The filters compare keys masked to filter_bits, as the kernels keep only 64 key bits, and the distinguished-point test precedes every escape and every look-ahead step; with check_all_replays every recorded trail is also replayed and any replay that misses its recorded point is counted. Reports the success rate against 1-exp(-tau), degenerate matches and replay mismatches. No oracle collision table. Toy scale only: it tests the procedure and its collision statistics, not production cost.

Check Lemma 1 of proof.md on random and edge-case Montgomery values: the 64-bit fraction approximations g_j are within [0,12] of floor(2^64*M(beta^j x)/p), and the kernel's rule for the canonical rotation either agrees with the exact minimum or falls back to the exact computation.
Recompute the claimed time_log2, preprocessing, memory and success lower bound from the stated parameters with exact integer arithmetic.
